deliverables: Milestone-based disbursement controls through TRSC/PSSC smart contracts
request.recipient: 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address stake1784sdxt6jjennmstphgdu7l7c2scf5d02a6cve2dgn5s2kq5u3j9v, with project funds later transferred to a Project-Specific Smart Contract; vendor named Teragone in prior funding disclosure.
request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Mithril Protocol continuous development through Intersect on behalf of the vendor.

claims.claim: Mithril addresses the cost and complexity of securely accessing and verifying Cardano blockchain state by using stake-based threshold multi-signatures to certify state in a trustless way.
The requested budget is 3,699,440 ada for Mithril Protocol Continuous Development plus a 110,983 ada Intersect Budget Administration fee, totaling 3,810,423 ada.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested withdrawal does not, at time of submission alone or in aggregate, breach the 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
Audit, administrative oversight, reporting obligations, and milestone-based disbursement controls are included through Intersect overhead and administration fees.
Treasury funds will be administered through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts, including one Treasury Reserve Smart Contract and one Project-Specific Smart Contract.
The Oversight Committee consists of Sundae Labs, Cardano Foundation, Dquadrant, NMKR, Sundial, and Eternl, and verifies key administrative actions using on-chain logic.
Teragone has not previously received direct funding from Cardano treasury or community governance programs, but has worked on Mithril for several years through IOG-funded collaboration.
Faster Mithril sync times lower onboarding friction and enable tooling for exchanges, wallets, monitoring, bridges, full wallets, light clients, and community-built tools.
The document states that the withdrawn funds can be tracked through a public dashboard and are immutably verifiable on-chain.

summary: The proposal requests 3,810,423 ada for Mithril Protocol continuous development and Intersect administration, citing Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, smart-contract-based treasury management, external oversight, and public tracking, but the anchor itself provides limited project summary, feasibility, risk, alternatives, failure-mode, and detailed budget analysis.
